newsitem.title: UK: All EU nations need intraday credit access - BoE.
newsitem.headline: All EU nations need intraday credit access - BoE.

text.p: Banks in all European Union nations should have equal access to intraday credit even if their countries have not signed up for a single European currency, Bank of England deputy governor Howard Davies said on Tuesday.
He said some people had argued banks in "out" countries should not have equal access to intraday credit in euros.

"The argument is that, if they do, credit in euros will be being created outside the euro zone, which would complicate monetary management," Davies said in a speech prepared for delivery to the British Computer Society.

But he said that view was mistaken. "It is perfectly possible to prevent any tangible spill-over from the settlement system into money supply creation by imposing penalties on overnight borrowing. "In other words, banks will need to settle up their positions at the end of the day, and pay heavily if they don't, which will surely encourage them to do so," he said.
Bundesbank deputy president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum said recently "outs" should not be given access to credit facilities of the European central bank.
But Davies said if the TARGET payments system, proposed for the European Union, was to operate efficiently, banks in all countries in the EU should have access to credit during the day.
